name: Mothman
habitat: Abandoned industrial zones and river valleys, especially around Point Pleasant, West Virginia.
description: A seven-foot winged figure with reflective red eyes. Precedes bridge collapses, bad storms, and other local disasters — or so the witnesses say.

name: Fresno Nightcrawler
habitat: Suburban lawns and parking lots of central California, always after midnight.
description: A pair of impossibly long legs with a small head on top. No arms. Walks like a pair of trousers that achieved sentience.

name: Chupacabra
habitat: Arid scrubland across Puerto Rico, Texas, and northern Mexico.
description: Goat-sucker. Livestock found drained of blood; witnesses describe spines, quills, or simply a mangy canid. The description drifts by zip code.

name: Jersey Devil
habitat: The Pine Barrens of New Jersey. Leeds family, thirteenth child, you know the story.
description: Kangaroo body, bat wings, horse head, forked tail. Three centuries of sightings and still no good photograph.

name: Bessie of Lake Erie
habitat: Lake Erie, favoring the South Bass Island shallows in late summer.
description: A thirty-foot serpent with a dog-like head. Surfaces for boaters, vanishes for decades. The lake keeps her secrets.

name: Bigfoot
habitat: Pacific Northwest old growth. Bluff Creek casts, Patterson–Gimlin country.
description: Eight feet of bipedal ape that smells like a wet sleeping bag. Leaves casts, knocks, and endless blurry footage.

name: Jackalope
habitat: Taxidermy shops and tall tales across Wyoming.
description: A jackrabbit with antelope horns. Loves whiskey, sings tenor, and was openly invented by two brothers in Douglas, Wyoming. Included here as our control sample: if the workflow verifies a jackalope, the workflow is broken.
